cohort: The study included 2,013,767 singleton, non-anomalous gestations delivered at 23-42 weeks in California from 2007 to 2011, of which 5,734 were complicated by urolithiasis.
finding: Urolithiasis during pregnancy was associated with 30% greater odds of preterm delivery and increased risk of various metabolic, hypertensive, and infectious disorders of gestation, and neonates born to these patients were more than twice as likely to develop neonatal abstinence syndrome.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly positively associated with urolithiasis during pregnancy.
followup_time: N/A (outcomes measured at delivery and in the neonatal period)
